Monica — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround on docs. A few clarifying Qs from our security team before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) BYOK scope: can ClearHealth bring its own CMKs (CMEK) for model inference at rest and for any long-term cached tokens? Does Redwood support customer-provided CMKs for both object storage and runtime key encryption?
2) HSM: is there an option to back CMKs with HSMs (CloudHSM / HSM appliance) rather than a software KMS key? We need attestation that keys never leave customer control.
3) Key rotation & dual-control: what are your recommended rotation intervals and do you support split-knowledge or dual-approval for exporting keys or rotating root material?
4) SOC 2 scope: does the SOC 2 Type II cover the hosted inference product and the console (user management, audit logs)? Is there a carve-out for third-party cloud providers?
5) HIPAA: do you have a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) and enumerated controls for PHI processing?

We already started the procurement side (Marie is copied). If you can get Rafael to respond to 1–3 in short bullets that’ll help us scope the tech call. Also please point to any public docs for CMEK/BYOK integration.

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS: follow-up, SOC2 docs, and next steps

Alex / Monica / Marie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; happy to expand on the tech call.

1) BYOK / CMEK support:
- Yes: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) for persistent storage (object stores, DBs where we store model artifacts and long-term caches) and for disk-level encryption in Private deployments. For Hosted (multi-tenant) we offer customer-isolated encryption via dedicated namespaces plus the ability to integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private modes.
- Implementation: we integrate with AWS KMS (CMEK) and GCP CMEK; for Dedicated/Private customers we can accept externally generated key material or configure a customer KMS endpoint.

2) HSM-backed keys:
- Yes: we support HSM-backed key material (CloudHSM / KMS with CloudHSM root) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted API customers, HSM-backed keys are available via Dedicated instances or via an enterprise key-provisioning flow that keeps key control within customer KMS.
- Attestation: keys are never exported from your KMS; Redwood only stores key references (key IDs). We can provide architecture diagrams and a short attestation statement under NDA.

3) Key rotation & dual-control:
- Rotation: we recommend 90–180 day rotation for CMKs depending on risk profile; automated rotation can be configured when using cloud KMS.
- Dual-control: for key material export or root operations, we support role-based approvals and can integrate with your approval workflows (via our RBAC + audit hooks). For highly regulated customers we offer a manual approval workflow (two-person approval) in Private installs.

4) SOC 2 scope & HIPAA / BAA:
- SOC 2 Type II: our latest attestation covers Redwood hosted inference and the Console services (user management, logging, and core control plane) for the environments listed in the report — we'll share the full attestation under NDA. Third-party cloud providers are listed as subservice organizations in the SOC 2 (standard carve-out language).
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for enterprise contracts; we have documented controls for PHI handling and will work with your legal team on the BAA scope.

Attachments & links we will send: 
- redwood_soc2_summary_2025.pdf (attached)
- redwood_encryption_whitepaper_v2.pdf (attached)
- Detailed architecture and KMS integration doc (we can share in the tech deep-dive or via secure link)

Next steps: 
- I recommend a 30-minute call where we walk through your questionnaire items and a short diagram of how BYOK/HSM would map to ClearHealth’s environment. Monica — please pick two times; Alex / Marie, we can also post a Loom diagram if that helps.

If helpful, we can also route a QSA-intake template for any compliance-specific requests.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
